transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Danielle. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Danielle, yeah, um, I'm having a real headache with one of our Wi-Fi mesh discs. The main hub downstairs is fine, but the upstairs pod just has this solid red light on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you get that mesh disc reconnected and working properly today, Bradley. May I take your account number to start?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure thing, it's SN 401 9820, under Bradley Turner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Bradley. For security verification, could you please confirm your full installation address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, it's 27 Oakfield Crescent, Stockport, SK4 3NX. And the PIN is 5192.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That has verified your details, thank you. You are on our Superfast Fibre 80 package with the Whole Home Wi-Fi guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's the one with the two white discs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to make sure I understand the issue: your primary Hub downstairs is broadcasting fine, but the secondary mesh pod upstairs is stuck on a solid red LED and won't connect devices, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly. And my teenage son is trying to study for his GCSEs in his back bedroom, and he has completely lost connection up there. It's causing absolute chaos this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how stressful that is, Bradley, especially with exam revision on the line. We will get that pod paired and his connection restored shortly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cheers Danielle, that would be a huge relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's diagnose where the signal is breaking down. Exactly where is that secondary disc plugged in upstairs right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on the landing, tucked just behind the large steel filing cabinet next to his bedroom door so the cables aren't visible.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A solid red light on the disc means it has completely lost contact with the 5 gigahertz backhaul channel from the primary hub downstairs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so it's not picking up the signal from downstairs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously, placing a radio antenna directly behind a solid steel cabinet creates an electromagnetic shield that blocks Wi-Fi signals entirely. It cannot penetrate sheet metal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, blimey. I didn't even think about the metal cabinet acting as a shield.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Metal is one of the worst Wi-Fi barriers. Was the disc working previously in that spot, or did you move it there recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We only tidied up the hallway yesterday afternoon and moved the cabinet and disc into that corner. It went red shortly after that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains the timing. I'd like to check our network telemetry to see the backhaul link quality recorded by the main Hub. Bear with me while I pull up the mesh logs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, no problem at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Bradley. Looking at the hub's Wi-Fi telemetry, the disc disconnected at 3:42 PM yesterday with a minus 88 dBm signal drop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, that matches right when we shifted the furniture around.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What we need to do is relocate the disc so it has an unobstructed line of sight down the stairwell or onto an open table in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There's a little wooden console table right at the top of the stairs, about two metres away from the cabinet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That wooden table sounds ideal. Wood does not absorb 5 gigahertz frequencies anywhere near as aggressively as metal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've unplugged the power lead from behind the cabinet. Walking over to the wooden console table now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Plug the power adapter into the wall socket near the console table and power on the disc, please.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Plugged in and clicked the power switch. The little LED on the front is pulsing purple now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Pulsing purple means it is booting up its internal operating system. That will take about thirty to forty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's just changed to flashing yellow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Flashing yellow indicates it is actively searching for the WPS synchronisation handshake from your main Hub downstairs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do I need to press the WPS button on the main router downstairs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Since it was already paired previously, it should automatically bind if the signal is clear. Let's watch it for another twenty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's still flashing yellow... wait, now it's gone flashing blue, and now it has turned solid blue!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Solid blue means an excellent backhaul connection to the primary Hub! Within about a minute, that will turn solid white for normal operation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it just flipped to solid white! That was quick.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to verify after that boot sequence, is the front LED maintaining a steady solid white light without dipping back to red?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, steady solid white. No flickering or red at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the disc on my controller dashboard now. It is linked with a minus 54 dBm signal strength, which is in the optimum green zone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant. Let me get my son to test his computer in the bedroom.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, please ask him to reconnect to the Wi-Fi network and confirm whether his devices roam onto the pod.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: He's just unlocked his laptop... full five bars of Wi-Fi showing! He's opening his school portal and an online video lecture.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you have him run a fast speed test on fast.com or our S-Net speed checker from his desk?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: He's running it right now... it's showing 76 megabits download and 19 megabits upload, with a 12 millisecond ping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is delivering 95 percent of your incoming line speed right to his study desk through the newly positioned mesh disc.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is absolutely fantastic! He's got his video lecture playing in HD with zero stuttering.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are any other devices in the upstairs bedrooms, such as tablets or smart TVs, showing full connection as well, Bradley?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my wife's iPad in the master bedroom has also picked up full signal from the landing disc. Everything upstairs is buzzing along.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to confirm, the upstairs mesh pod is firmly online, your son's revision is back on track, and all upstairs Wi-Fi connectivity is fully resolved?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 100 percent resolved. You've sorted the whole problem out in ten minutes. I'm so grateful, Danielle.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm delighted we could get that resolved for you and your son. I have saved notes on your account documenting the optimal disc placement on the console table.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We will definitely leave it right there on the wooden table and not put it near metal again!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, you can use the S-Net Home app to monitor the mesh signal strength anytime, which will alert you if any node moves out of range.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll download that onto my phone now, that's really handy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It lets you see connected client devices in real time and even run network health checks directly from your mobile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Super. That gives me great peace of mind while the kids are studying.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We also have automated channel optimization running in the background at 3:00 AM every morning to avoid neighbourhood radio congestion.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the system keeps itself tuned up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your broadband, landline or billing services that I can assist you with today, Bradley?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was everything. You've been brilliant Danielle, thanks again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome, Bradley. Please feel free to reach back out if you ever need any Wi-Fi guidance in future.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do. Have a great day!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Bradley. Best of luck to your son with his exams, and enjoy the rest of your week.
